criteria.note: Four parts. One written page: gap (six pages, oldest still a proposal, none covers stamina; docs/design/damage-model.md:3). Every number in data per fighter: gap (energy start, cap, regain and costs are code literals: sim/core/state.gd:1077, sim/core/fighter.gd:685,711,767; the energy model is on in the played build by a code patch, tools/preview/switches.mjs:918-919). Third fighter from data only: met for the sim (sim/core/tools/parity.gd:4162, CI run 42722446938), not evidenced for render and UI. No health bar, health reads from the fighter: met in the normal HUD (ui/widgets/ui_plate.gd:3; render/core/fighter_view.gd:266-284), with the F2 overlay's hit-point bar left (render/core/hud.gd:219-221) and readability not evidenced. The named tool, the two-fighter ratchet, exists and passes (365 of 365) but measures two-fighter spellings, not fighter-specific code; no tool counts energy literals; no read test exists. X-15 carries no proposed numbers; it should be read as including stamina (docs/ep/vision.md:1735).

not_evidenced: Q3 in part: whether a player can in fact read health and energy from the fighter at speed (no read test or record found)
Q4 in part: the UI feature flags inside Orb's packed build were not read (only main's ui/data/features.json)
Q6 in part: whether a third fighter needs data and art only in render and UI (proven for the sim only)
The exact count of energy literals in shipped sim code (lines cited, no full count)
CI on the baseline commit 8901d351 was still in progress when read (run 43554356718)

findings.s: No stamina and no "body" number exist in any code or data, so the energy, stamina and health loop Orb defined for Alpha is a plan only.
findings.orb: How much of the stamina, energy and body loop must be in Alpha? Recommendation: the whole loop as shared rules with per-fighter numbers in data, switched on only after QA's comeback measurement.
findings.vnote: No stamina exists in shipped code or data and the plan's body number is not built; the nearest thing is the old f.hp, a readout only since HP_ENDS_MATCH is false. X-13's text does not name stamina, so X-15 is the criterion that carries this.

findings.s: No single written page states the model: it is spread over six design pages, the oldest still a proposal that disagrees with the code on the brink, and none covers stamina.
findings.vnote: True in substance, but docs/design/spec-wounds.md is committed at the baseline (only a one-line local edit is uncommitted) and its line 15 already gives the brink as the core broken, so only damage-model.md:24 disagrees with the code. Stamina is touched in docs/design/melee-press-feel.md:181 and :202 (lunge prices), which is not a model page, so the main claim holds.

findings.s: Energy's own numbers (start, cap, regain, charge rate, hit gain, guard drain and the older costs) are literals in code, shared by every fighter, not data.
findings.vnote: Every cited line holds a bare number on ki (start 60, regain 5, cap 100, charge 30 a second, guard drain 0.08, hit gain 0.04, costs 4, 6, 40, 45). Only the neighbouring meter bonuses and the power ladder are read from data.

findings.s: The "one energy model" is off in the data on main and in both played builds, and is on in Orb's build only through a code patch the page tool writes, so main does not describe the game Orb played.
findings.vnote: All three data files say enabled false, and the page tool writes d["power"] = not pw_off into the match setup, which power.gd:118 reads ahead of the data. The build trees hold no render folder, so the patched line inside the builds could not be read directly; the claim rests on the tool's source.

findings.s: The backburnered hero and villain meters still change damage, energy regain, beam contests and where the computer leads the fight in every match, with no readout in the normal HUD.
findings.orb: The backburnered meters: switch off, fold in, or retire? Recommendation: keep the comeback as a rule for every fighter, zero every other effect in data now, remove the code after Alpha.
findings.vnote: The meters are read ungated at every cited line, and minimal_hud is true by default, which drops the meter from the plate. I did not trace whether the location read is switched on in data, so that clause is the least tested.

findings.s: The tool X-15 names does not measure X-15: the two-fighter ratchet counts four spellings of "exactly two fighters" and says nothing about fighter-specific code.
findings.vnote: The ratchet counts four spellings in shipped code and nothing else. A third-fighter-from-data test exists in parity.gd:4162 but is not the tool X-15 names, and no fighter-id lint was found in tools or CI.

findings.s: A health bar can still be put on screen: F2 swaps in the old overlay with a hit-point bar and MENACE or ANGUISH bars.
findings.vnote: True: F2 is handled in the shipped scene with no debug gate and the old overlay draws f.hp / f.maxhp as a bar. It is off by default and appears only on a function-key press or the legacy-hud argument, so the normal screen meets the criterion and this is a leftover to retire.

findings.s: No record shows that a player can read their own health, energy or readiness from the fighter at speed; the only energy readout found is the corner plate.
findings.vnote: No read test or record of one was found, so the main statement holds. The plate is not the only energy read: render/anim/anim_fighter.gd:2910-2911 puts a grounded fighter with ki under 6 into the winded idle pose, a narrow on-fighter cue for empty only.

findings.s: The HUD's power pip is computed at 25 per tier while the data's thresholds are 35, 65 and 100, so it reads full before a transformation is ready.
findings.vnote: The bridge is the only live writer of momentum and hard-codes 25 per tier while the sim reads thresholds [35, 65, 100] from data, so the tier-1 pip is full at power 25 (ready at 35) and later pips start part-full and fill early (50 vs 65, 75 vs 100). The transform prompt itself reads f.act.formReady, so only the pip misleads and minor holds.

findings.s: Body marks only grow to the worst stage reached and never fade, so the fighter cannot show recovery or the easing of injuries Orb wants from a new form.
A new kind of meter cannot be added as data: the loader accepts only the two backburnered meter names.
The old hit-point number is still tracked beside the wounds as a second health value, and QA's tools and three director files still read it.
findings.orb: Is "body" a new number, or the old hidden hit-point number renamed and reused? Recommendation: reuse it, so one deep health number sits behind the four body parts.

findings.s: Several damage numbers are code constants shared by all fighters: the stance table, combo growth, the charging penalty and five pinned wound values.
Render and content still key some looks and kit rows on a fighter's id, name or the words "hero" and "villain", so a third fighter is not proven to need data and art only outside the sim.
findings.vnote: Every cited line says what the finding says: outfit and seed keyed by roster id in a code const, cape/hair/gear keyed on the role words (line 220 is in the animated body's palette, so it reaches the shipped look), and kitFields keyed protagonist/rival. The glare's data override does not rescue it because data/vfx/glare.json does not exist, so the hard-coded name list runs; no code reads kitFields, so that row is content only.

findings.s: The Protagonist's own forms are off in data on main and in both played builds and the rival has no forms file, so "reaching new forms" is the shared four-tier ladder for both.
The rule that makes a match always end is off on main and on in Orb's build, so with hit points no longer ending a match, main's data alone does not guarantee an end.
Leftovers of hiding still sit in the energy and health code (faster regain and healing while hidden, x1.5 ambush damage), inert because no fighter can hide.

criteria.note: Per fighter 101 cells tabulated on main's data: 83 have an entry, 65 share an entry with another cell, 18 have none (reads/RR-01.md:219-224); LB, LT and RT face rows repeat the no-stance row. The coverage probe does not exist; nearest is sim/input/tools/audit_probe.gd. Proposed table: keep the shape but count cells on a signed list, since A has no mash or hold design in any stance.

Each pad drives its own fighter (render/core/main.gd:1350-1361; join_test 53 checks in docs/ep/runs/6a30b4c9/gate-full-s415.txt:94). Owner's last match: 1 stray beam of 8 (tick 5220, a refused stick beam fired 33 ticks later) and RT + B at tick 6617 outside the stated window (docs/qa/runs/6a30b4c9/README.md). The owner's named signature inputs do not exist, so the only signature input is RT + B. qa/godot/beam_trace.gd exists; the count over many matches is not built. Proposed count of 0: confirmed.

Save and load exist in code (user://ui_prefs.json via ui/hud/ui_hud.gd:2478,2485; user://input.json via sim/input/remap.gd:13, read at render/core/main.gd:153). No restart test on Windows desktop or Linux/Deck exists; nearest is a same-process reload in ui/tools/hud_check.gd:5913, not named in any workflow.

Q3 in part: settings surviving a restart on Windows desktop or a Deck
Q4 in part: player 1 starting on the left; a person's signed run of the two-pad checklist

findings.s: The owner's two signature inputs (RT + RB + a right-stick flick, RT + a right-stick flick) cannot be pressed: with RT held the right stick is switched off in the input layer, and the only signature input is RT + B.
findings.orb: Should RT + B stop being a signature once your two stick inputs exist? Recommendation: yes, retire RT + B so no beam can start from a face button.
findings.vnote: I tried RT + RB as a way round (mask 6 is not in inertMasks), but stance.gd:32-33 resolves any set with RT down to mask 4, which is inert on main and in both played builds. The only signature binding on the power layer is pad:east (B).

findings.s: Couch 2v2 with four pads cannot be played: the input hub holds two human slots per PC and every pad routine loops over two.
findings.vnote: The two-slot hub is as stated, but X-09 asks for the supported line-ups to be stated and lists two humans with two computer partners, which fits two slots. That couch 2v2 cannot be started at all is F-MODES-03's blocker; the hub limit alone only rules out three- and four-pad line-ups.

findings.s: Each fighter's move table has no outcome for 18 of 101 cells and 65 cells reach the same entry as another cell; the LB, LT and RT rows of the face buttons mostly repeat the no-stance row.
findings.vnote: The counts (101 cells, 18 not found, 65 sharing an id) and the LB, LT and RT rows reaching the no-stance ids match the record and the code lines. Caveat: this is a static reading of data and code, not the live scripted-pad probe X-03 names, and X-03's table is still marked proposed.

findings.s: A right-stick beam that is refused at release waits and fires by itself up to 90 ticks later, and did so in the owner's last match 33 ticks after the stick was let go, during a brawl started with a face button.
findings.vnote: The trace shows a heavy press at 5211 and a stick-beam exchange at 5220 with no stick down, and tryFire waits up to maxWaitTicks 90; nothing in sim or data changed after 6a30b4c9. Add that ownMove.enabled is false on main (interrupts.json:294), so the rule runs only where the page's switch table turns the beam move on, as in the played build.

findings.s: The pad as the owner plays it is not the default in data: eleven input switches are off on main and on in both played builds only through the private page's switch table.
findings.vnote: A key-by-key comparison gives exactly eleven switches false on main and true in both builds (driverOnRb, flightStrikeB, chordPick, dashHandover, flickKept, inertKnock, chargeLostCue, bNoBeam, bNoBeamKeepRt, hapticStages, dodgeHeld). Each has a false-to-true row in the page's switch table.

findings.s: A pad unplugged mid-match does not pause or show a notice: player two's fighter is handed to the computer and player one is moved to the keyboard while the match runs on.
findings.orb: When a pad drops out mid-match, should the game pause with a plain notice instead of handing the fighter to the computer? Recommendation: yes, pause in every local mode.
findings.vnote: No pause is right, but 'no notice' is wrong for player two: leave(1) adds a 'left' note (hub.gd:216) that the HUD shows as a brief line (render/core/main.gd:945, ui/hud/ui_hud.gd:2346). Player one's unplug goes through _free(0) with no note, and neither case is the pause with a plain notice X-07 asks for.

findings.s: The flight speed the owner preferred (3500) exists only as a slider on the private browser page; the data's default is 5000, the energy model that reads it is off on main, and the LAN setup sends no flight speed.
findings.orb: Should 3500 become the default flight speed for every mode, with the slider dropped until a real setting exists? Recommendation: yes.
findings.vnote: Default 5000, model off in data, and no flatOut key in any of the three LAN setups all hold; the played builds' power.json also say 5000. The only other reader of a flat-out word on main is a capture tool, not a player setting.

findings.s: The latest count of unanswered presses is from an older build: 225 of 760 presses not honoured (30 percent), 97 of them with no word or buzz, and no count exists for the build the owner last played.
findings.vnote: 760 presses, 225 not honoured (30%), and the silent column sums to 97; no ledger exists for 6a30b4c9 or its play files. Add that the ledger's own line 3 says the recorded match was not reproduced on that tree, so the rows are a replay that diverged from the played match.

findings.s: No moveset coverage probe exists: the nearest tool presses each input alone for 90 ticks and its saved result is from a tree of 1 November.
findings.vnote: No probe meets X-03, but 'each input alone' is wrong: audit_probe.gd:65-74 and 95-101 tap every face button under eight held layers (hold and mash only under none, LB, RB) and flick the stick per layer (104-109). It still falls short: one fighter (slot 0, line 161), 90 ticks, no empty or duplicate cell report, not in CI, and the only saved result is the 1 November s400 tree.

findings.s: The Steam Deck's built-in controls have never been tried: no run on a Deck or through Steam's pad layer is on record, and the project's own Deck page marks it untested.
findings.vnote: Every cited line says what the finding says and no record of a run on a Deck or through Steam's pad layer exists in the tree. The only Deck-specific code is a name match in pad_family that the Deck page itself says will usually not fire.

findings.s: The press-to-picture latency record is not current: it measures the browser build with keyboard presses on 22 and 23 October, before the right-stick scheme, and nothing measures a pad, the desktop build or a Deck.
findings.vnote: The bench sends keyboard events only on the web export, and responsiveness.md:66 says it was not rerun for the stick while line 18 says the 5-tick light start it recorded is gone. The 1 November numbers are headless native tick counts from synthetic input, not press-to-picture, so no pad, desktop or Deck on-screen measurement exists.

findings.s: The quick LT tap still carries the fighter further than the ruled step when far from the rival (9.9 body heights against a bound of 6.5), and was not measured against a moving rival.
With RT + B kept as the interim signature, B fires a signature for as long as RT is held and the fighter is not charging, not only in the first 12 ticks the rule's own comment states.
None of the 46 input test scripts runs in CI; the only saved run is the Executive Producer's local gate, where 45 ran and passed (the 46th file, mash_probe, is a probe).
Control and comfort settings are saved and reloaded in code, but no test restarts the game on Windows or Linux to prove it, and the saved-options load is skipped for scripted runs.
Keyboard play is bound for every action on the solo layout but is unproven on the played build, and two players on one keyboard get a weaker strike (one key plus the movement direction).
findings.orb: For Alpha, is 'keyboard works, a pad is recommended' enough, with full keyboard equality left for Beta? Recommendation: yes, since the outside testers play on a Deck.
findings.vnote: The shared keyboard gives each player one strike key plus the held movement direction, which the page itself calls lower than a pad, and keyboard is covered only by headless input tests with no played-build run on record. One small gap in 'every action': kb-solo has no hints binding (pause is the system key P, main.gd:1616).

findings.s: Leftovers stay live in the input layer: bindings and hints for three power specials that are switched off, a keyboard class nothing calls, and touch layouts and phone vibration while mobile is parked.
The controls folder's index is out of date and 51 parked paths sit uncommitted, some already on main, so the folder cannot be trusted to say what is landed.

criteria.note: Easy read 19/40 (47.5%) for the scripted Orb's-scheme player on the tree that became 6a30b4c9 (docs/director/runs/6eec6a75/hitstop-row/final/table.txt:4), under Game Design's band of at least 70% (docs/design/gauntlet-plan.md:22). Medium and Hard: no record since 2026-11-01 (not evidenced). No run on packed data. The scripted player exists (tools/feel/gauntlet.gd:187-206, --level) but is Tools', not QA's, not in CI, and models only flicks and guard. Recommended bands from the record: Easy at least 70%, Medium 35 to 60%, Hard at most 20%, 100 matches a cell (40 is good to about 15 points).

No enemy control for many weak enemies: henchmen are paper only (docs/combat/henchmen-grades.md:3), the one-versus-many ring is parked and not on main, a match holds five bodies at most with no waves or respawn (sim/core/roster.gd:36-40). The frame-rate half is not measurable until a wave exists; mode smoke missing (F-MODES-09).

not_evidenced: Q1 (part): win rates on the played build's packed data, and any Medium or Hard win rate since 2026-11-01; the cause of the 65% to 45% Easy drop
Q2 (part): how often the computer perfect-blocks charged attacks on the played build (last measured 2026-10-16, about 6%)
Q3 (part): whether the computer uses the two signature inputs, the gravity well and every move-table cell; whether it ever fires a beam by an input a player lacks on the played build
Q5 (part): how good a computer ally is (no human-plus-computer team has been set up or measured)
Q4 (part): whether the parked ring still applies to main, and what bodies past the second do on main today

findings.s: There is no computer control for many weak enemies: henchmen are paper only, the one-versus-many director (the ring) is parked and not on main, and a match holds five bodies at most with no waves or respawn.
findings.vnote: The ring class exists only in the parked folders, main's guards stand until stage 2, the cap is 5 bodies, and nothing in game code or data spawns waves or henchmen. X-10 cannot be met as main stands, so blocker holds by the rule.

findings.s: Easy is too hard for a scripted player using Orb's scheme: it won 19 of 40 (47.5%) on the tree that became the played build, against Game Design's band of at least 70% and the criterion's proposed 60 to 80%.
findings.orb: How hard should Easy be for someone playing your way? Recommendation: keep Game Design's bar of at least 7 wins in 10 and tune Easy to it.
findings.vnote: final_orbs reads 19/40 at easy and both bands read as stated; the build's own data has the same two switches on (pace matching, budgetAny) as the cell. No later easy record for this pad exists.

findings.s: Medium and Hard have no win-rate record for Orb's scheme on any build since 2026-11-01; the only figures on a design page are 0 wins at each level from 10 matches.
findings.vnote: Records since 2026-11-01 do exist: Orb's scheme won 0% of 40 at medium and at hard on build 1931a0f8's own tree (docs/tools/runs/1931a0f8/b1-gauntlet.txt:5-6, 2026-11-08) and 0 of 10 each on e80b8e3d (docs/tools/gauntlet-orbs-scheme-e80b8e3d.md:18-19); the reading RR-06 searched only docs/director/runs and docs/qa/runs. What holds is that neither level has a record on the played build 6a30b4c9 or any tree with pace matching and the hit-stop change.

findings.s: No win rate has been measured on the played build's own packed data: every record was made on a scratch tree with patches laid on, by a Tools script that is not in QA's folder or in CI.
findings.vnote: "Every record was made on a scratch tree with patches" is wrong: docs/tools/runs/1931a0f8/b1-gauntlet.txt:1 was run on an earlier build's own tree (orb-first-play-1931a0f8-7a5a2d2c/tree). The core holds: no win rate is on record for the played build 6a30b4c9's packed data, and the gauntlet is a Tools script in neither qa/ nor CI.

findings.s: Main's computer-opponent data is not the played build's: Easy's pace matching, the beam pacing against a human, and the computer's hold-and-release beam are on in the build and off on main.
findings.vnote: All three switches (vsHuman, easy paceMatch, ownMove.enabled and ownMove.ai) read false on main and true in the build's tree, as cited. It follows the team's switch-list practice, but a candidate cut from main's data would play a different opponent than the one measured and played.

findings.s: The computer never throws a right-stick strike, the main attack of Orb's scheme: the only right-stick input the computer writes is the beam's hold.
findings.orb: Should the computer use the right-stick strikes in Alpha? Recommendation: yes at Medium and Hard, built before the final difficulty tuning.
findings.vnote: The only computer writes to right-stick fields are the beam's start, hold and release, and the stick strike is its own class of blow (stick.gd:4), so the computer's light and heavy do not stand in for it. X-13's wording does not itself ask this of the computer; the weight rests on Orb's rule at vision.md:608.

findings.s: No standing check proves the computer uses only inputs a player has: on main its signature is still the old B request that locks its rival, the hold-and-release check is local only, and no record of it exists for the played build.
findings.vnote: With ownMove.ai false on main, aiStart returns false and the computer sets i.sig, the old request; beam_ai_check is in no CI step and its only logs are on earlier scratch trees, none on 6a30b4c9. The played build has the switch on, so the gap is main's data plus a missing standing check, not the build's behaviour.

findings.s: There is no computer ally: the only 2v2 line-up puts both computers on the enemy team, and no menu or host can start a match with a computer on a human's side.
findings.orb: Is a computer partner part of Alpha's 2v2? Recommendation: yes, one line-up (one human and a computer partner against two computers) so a solo tester can play 2v2.
findings.vnote: Teams are slots 0 and 2 against 1 and 3, and the one line-up has computers on 1 and 3 only; no menu, page or host outside checks starts a four-slot match. The sim would accept a computer on slot 2 (sim.gd:42), so what is missing is a way to start it and any record of it played.

findings.s: Matches against Easy run long: the scripted Orb's-scheme player's 40 matches averaged about 576 seconds and the masher's about 426, against the criterion's normal match of 6 to 8 minutes.
findings.vnote: The averages hold (1,383,534 ticks/40/60 = 576.5 s; 1,021,345/40/60 = 425.6 s), but 426 s is 7.1 minutes, inside the 6 to 8 minute band (median 345.3 s is under it), so only the Orb's-scheme arm runs long (9.6 min mean, median 548.5 s). The criterion text is at alpha-audit-specification.md:180 (X-13), not :175 (which is X-08), and the record is a patched replay tree on 6eec6a75, not the played build's packed data.

findings.s: The computer's level is one value for the whole match, not one per fighter, so an ally weaker or stronger than the enemy, or graded enemies, cannot be set.

The fix for Orb's remark that the computer perfect-blocks charged attacks too easily is parked and not on main: its data key is in the schema but in no data file and no code, and the rate is unmeasured on the played build.
The checks of the computer opponent run by hand only: the level check, the pace check, the computer-beam check and the 2v2 partner check are not in CI, and no CI job reads a win-rate band.
Forty matches a cell cannot tell neighbouring bands apart (about 15 points either way), and the drop the EP flagged, 65% to 45% for Easy, is inside that noise and was read on two different trees.
Backburnered ideas are still in the computer's decisions: it picks where to lead the fight from the hero and villain meters, and its hiding choices remain in code though no fighter can hide.
findings.vnote: The roam is called live (ai.gd:180) and takes its role from which meter a fighter has (location.gd:116-118), both fighters have canHide false while ai.gd:108-111 keeps the hiding weights, and the meters are on the backburner list (vision.md:1735). Nuances: the roam reads the meter's presence, not its value, and the tie to X-15 is loose (the specification's question at :364 fits better).

findings.s: Some of the computer's numbers are constants in code, not data: how often an attack beat attacks, the share of heavies, the blind swing and the lull limit.
The scripted Orb's-scheme player is a narrow model of the scheme: right-stick flicks and a held LB guard only, and it fired no beam in 40 matches while Easy fired 459.
The parked one-versus-many work was last rebuilt on 2026-10-16 and applies by exact-text patches; whether it still applies to today's director code is not evidenced.

criteria.note: No planet picker and no size, city, climate or water setting (sim/world/planet.gd:328 takes a seed only; sim/core/constants.gd:21 fixes the size; render/core/main.gd:441-442); LAN fixes planet 7 (net/lan.gd:30). Same seed, same planet holds within one platform (planet_check vectors pass in CI run 43553420852, Linux); Windows against Linux is not evidenced. Tool exists in part: planet_digest.gd prints fingerprints with no verdict and is left out of CI (tools/world-checks.json:32).

Base-tier fights barely touch buildings in the saved record (at most 1.7% of structure mass at tier 1 over 22 AI matches, docs/world/runs/c7b0414b/structure-mass-by-tier-matches.txt, uncommitted, taken on a pre-landing stack); terrain not measured. The proposed 3 times width is not met for the same blow (1.32 times for an impact, crater.gd:55 and :87-89; 1.48 for a shot, blast.json tierEnergy), only for powering up (about 9 times, crater.gd:56-57). No check asserts a ratio (blastcheck prints only). Recommend restating as 2.5 times the width for a top-power send against a base send, measured with the energy model on, and 3% structure mass as the base-tier cap.

Q8 in part: the cause of Orb's 'hump of ocean water' (candidate only, unchecked)
Q2 in part: whether step 0's other tools (QA's outcome counter, Rendering's drawn-versus-stood probe) exist
Q1 in part: the plan's claims that heaps, banks, trees and fight water slide with the line were not re-checked in code

findings.s: On main the round planet is not the game's world: a match with no planet setup key plays the old hand-made arena, the menu never sets that key, and Orb's globe build gets it from a preview patch plus world data switches that main ships off.
findings.vnote: No planet key means WorldTerrain.genBegin (the hand-made world), planet_part's own comment says the menu has no such choice yet, and planet is not a URL word on main; the build's data has water on and gen 2 where main has off and gen 1. Two routes on main do reach a planet that the finding does not name (LAN's fixed planet 7 at net/lan.gd:30, and the local-only --tiles switch at tile_ground.gd:105-106), but neither is the menu, so the statement holds.

findings.s: Custom planet setup has nothing under it: the generator takes a seed only, the planet's size is a constant, and city count, climate and water are fixed numbers in data files, not match settings (same gap as F-MODES-07).
findings.orb: For Alpha, is a seed plus three dials (city count, climate, water) at today's one size enough, with sizes after Alpha? Recommended: yes.
findings.vnote: The planet is memoised by seed and generation only, PLANET_NC is a constant, cities are 12 in data and no setup key for size, cities, climate or water exists in code. findings.s: Developer keys are live in every build with no switch, and three change flashing: F8 brings back the flash shapes from before Legal's conditions unless a lock flag that is off on main is on, Alt with a key fires any registered flash on demand, and F7 toggles the fighters' flashes.
findings.vnote: The keys are live with no switch, but every packaging path (desktop package, LAN kit, site export) sets the lock on, so F8 is refused in a build a tester gets, and Legal's record has F8's shapes measured with no trigger. Alt with a key and F7 stay open and unmeasured, though a fired flash still passes its cooldown and pulse grant.

findings.s: Making the Rail the default is unfinished: its switch is off on main, three older HUD checks fail with it on, Tools' smoke test clicked the wrong place on it, its checks leave out 1280 by 800, and only its Start screen has a saved still.
findings.orb: Are the Rail menus the Alpha's menus? Recommended: yes, once the pause fault is fixed and the screens are checked at the Deck's size.
findings.vnote: Switch off, three failures with it on, no 1280 by 800 case and a single still all hold. The smoke mis-click is already fixed: the same record says the click at (1133, 651) was added and the re-run passed, and it is on main at tools/preview/smoke.mjs:110.

findings.s: The Rail's match-over screen is a full-height panel over the left 30% of the screen, which is where player one's plate, portrait and spoken lines sit; no still of it is on file.
findings.orb: When a match ends, where should the result panel sit? Recommended: keep it off the winner's corner (for one player, off your own).
findings.vnote: The rail is a full-height rectangle from the left edge, and the team's own owed list says it covers the left portrait and line; only the Start still is on file. The width is 30% only up to a 480-pixel cap, so at 1920 wide it is 25% (ui_rail.gd:44).

findings.s: The start menu's d-pad behaves unevenly, as Orb reported: Up from the top row jumps to Start while Down from the bottom row stops, and Left or Right on the Players row swaps the row two below it between the computer's level and player two's device (by reading; not reproduced).
findings.vnote: Pad Up from the first row jumps to the last row while Down clamps, and the third row is the computer's level or player two's device by the Players value. The keyboard's Up does not wrap, a further difference.

findings.s: The feedback panel cannot be worked with a pad: a pad's only actions there are B or Start to close, so tags, Copy and Save need a mouse or a touch and the note needs a keyboard.
findings.vnote: The panel's pad branch acts on B and Start only and marks every other pad button handled; tags and buttons are reached only through the mouse-click branch. I found no other pad handler for the panel.

findings.s: The tool that makes a report folder is the owner's own Windows tool: it needs this repository and Node, writes a .cmd shortcut only and has no size cap, and nothing packs a tester's report on Linux or tells them where the file is.
findings.orb: Should a tester's report be one small file they post themselves, with clips left out? Recommended: yes, one file under 10 MB saved by one press in every build.
findings.vnote: The tool is Node in this repository, writes a .cmd, zips with PowerShell, prints the zip's size and has no cap, and nothing exists for Linux. The claim that nothing tells a tester where the file is is wrong for a LAN build: the game names the saved file and the pause screen says reports go in the 'saved' folder beside the game (terms.json:94, ui_hud.gd:2148).

findings.s: Other developer keys reach a tester too: F2 swaps in the grey-box HUD with MENACE and ANGUISH bars, seed and tick text and a plain pause with no menu, F3 shows a performance overlay, F4 the debug feed and F6 turns effects off.
findings.vnote: The key handler has no build or debug gate (only a loading/boot return), so F2, F3, F4 and F6 all work in a shipped build. F2 hides UI's HUD, makes pause a bare host.paused flip, and the grey-box HUD draws seed/tick text and MENACE/ANGUISH bars.

findings.s: Two keyboard keys do something a tester won't expect: F9, which the game teaches as the report key, also switches the split screen on or off in the host, and Escape during play closes the desktop game at once with no question.
findings.vnote: The HUD's _input saves the report on F9 without marking the key handled, so main's _unhandled_input also attaches or detaches the split view (split_view exists by default). Escape reaches get_tree().quit() on desktop whenever no HUD screen is open to consume it.

findings.s: How to play's Reading the fight page describes things the minimal HUD no longer draws (a ring that flashes on a hurt body, finishing-move rings, the planet strip, a box at the top that counts damage), and nothing filters those lines out.
findings.vnote: The four lines are on the Reading the fight page and the layers they describe are switched off by minimal_hud (true in features.json). ui_howto.gd filters on other flags but never mentions minimal_hud.

findings.s: X-22 cannot be measured today: there is no still of any screen at 1280 by 800 and no tool that sweeps every screen at that size, only plan-level checks of the older layout.
findings.vnote: 1280 by 800 appears only as a size in plan-level checks, and the Rail's own size list at hud_check.gd:10824 leaves it out; text_size_check never mentions the Rail. No tracked still and no sweep tool at that size exists.

findings.s: X-20 has no test of its own: saving and loading are checked only inside one headless process, never across a restart or on Linux, a failed write is silent, and no page says where the two files live on each platform.
findings.vnote: Both round trips run in one process against test paths and neither they nor remap_test run in CI, so no restart or Linux case is exercised; the prefs write ignores a failed open. The only mention of the save folder is a Windows aside in a QA run note, not a page covering both platforms.

findings.s: No UI check runs in CI: the 8,288-check HUD suite, the text-size check and the overflow check are run by hand only, so a menu regression can reach a build unseen.
findings.vnote: No workflow runs any UI check; the 8288 figure matches the gate record. The hand-run gate script does run hud_check but not the text-size or overflow checks, which softens the risk slightly without changing the fact.

findings.s: The teaching for transformations, specials, brace and vanish is switched off until those presses are real, and nothing on screen or in How to play names the signature inputs Orb set for Alpha.
findings.vnote: forms_live, specials_live, brace_live and vanish_live are all false and the page drops or rewrites those lines. The only signature row is 'Big blow' on the bound button; nothing names the trigger-plus-stick-flick inputs recorded at vision.md:1710.

findings.s: Settings lists two rows that do nothing in this build: Beat ring, which the minimal HUD never draws even when on, and Show recipe, whose readout is a placeholder with no drawing.
First-time help is the How to play card and one-line hints only; the guided first match is a proposal from September with nothing built.
Leftovers of the backburnered hero and villain meters and of hiding remain in the UI code and words, switched off or unseen under the minimal HUD.

Three UI pages or headers state a status the code has moved past: the minimal HUD page and the report page say parked or off while their switches are on, and the prefs file's header says it holds one value while it holds the options and menu choices.

criteria.note: No Alpha match checklist probe exists (git grep in qa, tools, sim found none). From the audio side: three pillar moments (building damage, bystanders, gravity well) have no sound in any build and four (beam, launch, knock-out, transformation) have one only with sound sets that are off on main. X-13 as written does not ask that a pillar be heard. No audio number in the criterion to confirm or change.

not_evidenced: Q2 in part: whether Orb's 2026-11-09 crackle remark is about the fixed build, and whether a real pad press starts sound in the browser
Q6: sound on Linux and the Steam Deck (and on any desktop build) is not evidenced

findings.s: On main five sound sets are off, so a build made plainly from main has no beam, knock-out, launch, struggle or transformation sound; Orb's build has three of them on only through build switches.
findings.vnote: All five sets are enabled=false on main and only tug, moments and carry are on in the 6a30b4c9 pack; no switch row exists for coop or world. Nuances: the launching or finishing blow still plays its ordinary hit, the struggle itself is also off on main (interrupts.json:273), and `transform` stays silent even with the sets on (first-play-sound.md:49).

findings.s: No sound exists for a building being damaged or collapsing, bystanders scattering, the gravity well, or any menu action, and the fight has no ambience or music bed in any build.
findings.orb: Is a dry fight (no ambience, no music) acceptable for Alpha? Recommendation: add one quiet ambience bed and the building and menu sounds; leave bystanders and the gravity well for later.
findings.vnote: No handler or sound id exists for building damage or collapse, bystanders, the gravity well or menus, and Audio's own page says no music or UI sound was ever made. Ambience beds exist as data and code (17 beds) but are off on main and not switched on in Orb's build, so the 'in any build' wording holds.

findings.s: Nothing in the area is proved by ear: Audio's pages say nobody has listened, and Orb's latest word (2026-11-09) is that the crackles sounded bad, with no record of whether that was the fixed build.
findings.orb: Will you do one ten-minute listening pass on a desktop build before testers get it? Recommendation: yes.
findings.vnote: 'Nothing is proved by ear' is too wide: Orb has listened and reported that sound plays (vision.md:1646 'sound worked'; vision.md:1705 'the beeps worked') and gave tone notes on 2026-10-16 (vision.md:1333-1334, brawl-beat.md:5). What holds is that no sound has the owner's approval by ear, Audio cannot listen, and the crackle remark at vision.md:1703 names no build.

findings.s: Sound on the Alpha's platforms (a Windows desktop build, Linux, the Steam Deck) is not evidenced: every proof is the browser build in Chrome, the only audio project setting is web-only, and no CI job runs an audio check.
findings.vnote: The gap holds: no record of sound heard on a desktop, Linux or Deck build, the only audio project setting is web-only (project.godot:14), and no CI job runs an audio check. One fact is wrong: the proof is not Chrome only, since vision.md:1705 records sound in Firefox on the old PC, though that is still the browser build.

findings.s: There is no music: no track has been handed back, the encoder install was not approved, and the pipeline has never run end to end.
findings.orb: Does Alpha need music? Recommendation: no; ship with a quiet ambience bed and run the music test after Alpha.

findings.s: Stacked impacts overdrive the engine's limiter (peaks +1.1 to +9.3 dBFS before it) on the mixer path a desktop build uses, and the resulting distortion was never measured or heard.
The pad-only silent start in the browser is half fixed: the engine-side hook and the start-menu line that warns the player are parked, and the getter built for it is read by nothing.
Legal's ruling on the music tool rests on summaries of its terms read on 2026-10-04, and says so; no re-read is recorded before a track would ship to outside testers.
No audio check runs in CI, and two sound data files (co-op and moments) have no schema rule, so a broken cue file would only warn.

Leftovers: the caption babble voice is unreached by the game, a schema rule points at a music file that does not exist, and nine audio parks stay on disk although two are fully on main and one is withdrawn.

criteria.note: 1v1 and team 2v2 matched every state check on two real Windows PCs on older builds (a8bc66e2, 091dfac9), but the played build 6a30b4c9 has only in-program rows, 2v2 apart was never played on two PCs, there is one match per launch, the gone-PC rule is 8 s (net/lan.gd:45) against the proposed 5 s, and no pulled-cable trial exists. Tools: the LAN log's state checks and saved matches exist; the report folder exists but is unproven on a real save; a pulled-cable trial is missing. Proposed numbers: keep five matches each; change 5 s to 10 s (or lower the constant) because the hand-over to the computer cannot be undone.

Met in part: a replay is refused on another format, input version or data hash (sim/core/replay.gd:116-136), LAN saves carry the build commit (net/lan.gd:511) and CI plays saved matches back. Missing: a build id inside the replay, refusal of a same-data build with different code, a plain message to the player (not evidenced), and any real LAN save verified.

not_evidenced: Q1 in part: which mode the 2026-11-08 two-PC session played, and any two-PC play on the played build 6a30b4c9
Q2 in part: a Windows-against-Linux match on exported builds has never been run; no record states whether cross-platform LAN is expected at Alpha
Q4 in part: whether the firewall rule stops Windows' own prompt
Q5 in part: no real LAN save or report folder exists to check

findings.s: No LAN match on the played build (6a30b4c9) has a record from two real PCs: its only LAN records are nine rows with the second PC simulated inside one program, and the real two-PC logs kept are from two older builds.
findings.vnote: The 6a30b4c9 record is nine --lan-loop rows with the other PC in the same process (no socket opened), and the only real-link logs kept are in the a8bc66e2-c and 091dfac9 folders. No lan-*.json save and no later LAN record for 6a30b4c9 exists anywhere I could find.

findings.s: An outside tester could not set up LAN without help: the folder is built on the hosting PC with that PC's address written into the shortcuts, needs an administrator firewall step, runs an unsigned Windows program, and its own words allow only Orb and Orb 2 to play.
findings.orb: Does LAN stay with Orb and Orb 2 only for Alpha? Recommended: yes; outside testers get the solo and same-PC modes.
findings.vnote: Every cited line says what the finding says: the kit refuses an address that is not the building PC's own, the shortcuts carry it, the firewall script elevates, and the words name the unsigned build and limit play to Orb and Orb 2. No other route to LAN exists, since every desktop preset excludes net/.

findings.s: There is no LAN build for Linux or the Steam Deck and no Windows-against-Linux match has ever been run, so cross-platform LAN at Alpha is unproven and today impossible.
findings.orb: Should a Windows PC be able to play a Steam Deck over LAN at Alpha? Recommended: no, Windows to Windows only; run one no-network comparison between a Windows PC and a Deck to keep the door open.
findings.vnote: The kit exports only the Windows preset to an .exe and the Linux preset excludes net/. CI's two-process ENet check is Linux against Linux on one machine and the two-PC check was Windows against Windows, so no cross-OS match is on record.

findings.s: A PC that falls silent is declared gone after 8 seconds, not the 5 seconds X-08 proposes, and no pulled-cable test on two real PCs is on record.
findings.orb: How fast must 'the other PC has gone' appear? Recommended: within 10 seconds, keeping today's 8-second rule.
findings.vnote: A silent link is declared gone after DROP_MS = 8000 ms and the banner follows that; only a closed link is noticed sooner. The only drop test is in-process with a 1 s threshold, and no real-PC pulled-cable record exists.

findings.s: Every LAN status except a dropped PC (waiting, could not connect, could not start, out of step, match over) is shown only in the window's title bar, and a detected state mismatch writes no report of its own.
findings.vnote: Match over is not title-only: the game's own MATCH OVER card shows too, though the words admit it may show on one PC only (net/tools/lan_words.txt:38). The rest holds: the other statuses go only to the title and the log, and NetDesync.writeReport is called only from the check tool, so a mismatch saves nothing of its own.

findings.s: The report folder from both PCs has never been made from a real LAN save, and its shortcut needs Node and this repository at a fixed path on the main PC plus a hand copy of the second PC's files.
findings.vnote: The doc says outright that no real LAN save exists, and none is on disk. The shortcut calls node on an absolute path into this repository and tells the player to copy the old PC's files over by hand.

findings.s: LAN play reaches the game only through text patches the kit makes to a scratch copy of two game files, and neither the kit nor the patched game's real window, menu and pads are run by CI.
findings.vnote: The kit edits more than two files: sim_host.gd and main.gd, plus meteor.gd, audio_coop.gd, interrupts.json, features.json and export_presets.cfg (net/tools/lan_kit.mjs:43-101). The substance holds: CI runs only lan_check (game side, no socket) and never the kit, the patched build, its window, menu or pads.

findings.s: A replay carries a hash of its data, its format and its input version but no build id, so a replay from a build with the same data and different code is run and fails at a checkpoint instead of being refused with a plain message.
findings.vnote: The replay header and SimReplay.play hold no build id, as stated, but the LAN save file does carry build.commit beside the replay (net/lan.gd:511) and Tools' clip tool refuses a file with no kept build of that commit (docs/tools/lan-report.md:18, not :17). Nothing in the game or in blackbox-verify reads it, so a same-data foreign replay still runs and fails at a checkpoint.

findings.s: LAN 2v2 has been played on two real PCs only in its team form and only on the 2026-11-07 build; the apart form has no real two-PC record on any build.
findings.vnote: The owner's words at vision.md:1662 say the together form was the only 2v2 tried, no later record shows an apart match on two PCs, and the apart rows for 6a30b4c9 are simulated in-program. Caveat: LAN logs do not record the mode (every mode uses seed 77), so the 2026-11-08 match on 091dfac9 cannot be shown to be 1v1 or 2v2 from files, and the cited log alone does not prove 'team form'; vision.md does.

findings.s: The handshake refuses a proposed input wait above 8 ticks but not a negative one, which by the code leaves this PC on Waiting for ever with no failure message (traced in code, not run).
The LAN link is plain, unencrypted ENet, which is acceptable on a home network and must change before any internet play.
The corrective plan's row for hardening the LAN link has an empty status cell although the delay cap, the packet checks and the dropped-PC handling are in the code and in CI.
The determinism lint has no rule for the engine's pow, exp or log, so a future bare use in the sim would pass it; none is in the sim today.
The Web export preset does not leave out the network folder, so the browser build's pack carries the unreached network scripts, including 26 test scripts.
findings.vnote: The Web preset leaves net/* in (the Windows preset at line 55 leaves it out) and nothing outside net/ calls it, so the substance holds. The count is wrong: the page's pack carries 26 packed files for 13 test scripts (a .gdc and a .gd.remap each, pck-vs-page.txt:15-41), not 26 test scripts.

findings.s: Groundwork for online play (a spectator, a seat take-over proposal, a rollback bench that estimates a phone) sits in the network folder with CI time spent on it but no Alpha use.

criteria.note: Animation half is mostly met in data: every strike piece Combat names resolves to the fighter's own key set (79 of 79 Protagonist, 80 of 84 rival; four tail strikes waiting), but the cells themselves are incomplete (F-COMBAT-04) and nothing measures it live. Keep COMBAT's corrected table (X, Y, B three ways, A two) and count animation per piece in a cell's pool, since 65 of 83 cells share a pool. The live probe does not exist (F-COMBAT-11); a data half exists (render/anim/tools/coverage.gd with docs/animation/launch-pair-coverage.json) but is stale since 2026-10-03 and in no gate.

Three steps beyond base are reachable for both fighters on the shared ladder (data/fight/ladder.json:10), so the proposed 'at least two' can be raised to three, matching Orb's 'about three'. 'The change is visible' is met by the aura only: same three placeholder poses for every form and fighter, no body look per form (F-ANIM-01). No transformation probe exists; a picture tool render/vfx/tools/transform_shots.gd exists (not opened, in no gate) and could give the still per form.

Q2 in part: whether any bent limb is still visible in build 6a30b4c9 (no anim_check or joint_scan record on the landed tree; no later complaint from Orb on file)
Q4 in part: what each tier looks like on each fighter on screen (no still read)

findings.s: A transformation changes only the aura: both fighters play the same three placeholder poses for every form and no body look is keyed to a form.
findings.orb: Is an aura change enough for a transformation in Alpha, or must the body change too? Recommendation: one cheap body change per step carried by data (hair or accent colour and each fighter's own break pose), bulked-up bodies after Alpha.
findings.vnote: The three poses are keyed by version (full, short, live), not by fighter or form, the settle eases back into the fight, and the body mesh is cached by a palette built once from col, hair and lane colour with no tier or form input. The only tier reads on the fighter are the aura's size and its streaks at tier 3 and up (fighter_view.gd:458-465); forms are also off on main (data/fight/forms.json:4).

findings.s: In a 2v2 the two copies of each fighter are drawn identically, and the mirror match is held off for the same missing second colour.
findings.orb: In a 2v2, how should the second copy of a fighter differ? Recommendation: a second body colour per fighter from Art, picked by team, not a marker over the fighter.
findings.vnote: A default 2v2 is the roster's first two, twice; each copy takes the same col, aura and hair, and the lane remap is keyed by aura hex for fighters 0 and 1 only, so both copies get the same palette, and fighter-select.md:26 holds the mirror match for a second lane colour. X-08 and X-09 as written test state mismatch and pad line-ups, not telling copies apart, so the criterion link is loose though major still fits.

findings.s: The animation check that holds the joint gate is in no CI job and has no saved record on the tree that was landed as 6a30b4c9.
The animation coverage table is of 2026-10-03, was built from Combat's then-parked files, still marks 180 of 228 rows parked, and its check runs in no gate.
The creative rulebook's held-pose rows still fail the animation check, which is a line of the EP's full gate, against the project rule that they never block a gate.
findings.orb: Should a failed held-pose rule stop a change from landing? Recommendation: no, report it as a warning and keep only the joint limits as a hard stop.

findings.s: The rulebook's three questions to Orb (which numbers move, a named-exception list, who signs a change) are unanswered, so every threshold is still Legal's first guess.
The animation runtime, its tools and its data (render/anim, data/anim) are on no director's owns line; Animation owns only art/animation and docs/animation.
The rival's four tail strikes sit in his live pools as waiting rows with no key set and no tail bones in the rig.
Animation's parked-work page still says Parked for patches the inventory found on main, and the wave files' own headers still say no live match plays them.

findings.orb: Will you mark a short list of the text a tester meets (notice, start menu, how-to card, match-over card, report panel) before outside testers play? Recommendation: yes, about 150 strings, not all 1115.

findings.orb: Should Grist and Loupe speak their approved lines in the Alpha? Recommendation: yes, switched on in the tester build once captions are checked on the Deck's screen.

The how-to card names keyboard keys to a pad player: its corner hint reads "Enter: next   Esc: close" whenever touch is off, and its reopen line says "the pause menu or F1".
The title is shown and stamped as plain "Orb Combat EX" with no working-title mark, while Legal's page says the visible heading may keep "(working title)" until the search is done.

findings.s: The desktop package rules were written for private test builds and conflict with an Alpha on itch.io: files are kept one day, the run is deleted after hand-over, no link or mention is allowed, the approval must be under 30 days old, and network play must be absent.

findings.s: A build carries a commit and a date but no version number, the Windows program's version fields are empty, no changelog file exists, and whether the game shows its build stamp on screen outside the report is not evidenced.

findings.s: The Godot check job's time swings from about 35 to 62 minutes on unchanged game code against a 75-minute limit, and the network job has reached 86% of its 60 minutes, so a slow runner or a few new checks turns a clean commit red and blocks the deploy.
findings.vnote: Times and limits are as cited, but 'unchanged game code' is wrong for the 62 to 35 minute span: 3a979379 to 6d2e17e0 is the Monday polish batch (43 game files, 2214 lines added); only 1fd23fa2 to 3a979379 was unchanged and both took about 61 minutes. The swing is real, but a job that outruns its limit is cured by a re-run or a larger limit, so it is a nuisance rather than a bad Alpha.

findings.s: The checks that plan every screen at 1280 by 800 exist but run in no CI job, and no saved record or set of stills shows the menus free of clipped or overlapping text at the Deck's size.

findings.s: Sounds are captioned for two cues only (the beam struggle and an opening), and that caption line is off by default, so a player who cannot hear gets no words for other sound cues.
Corrective item CD-14 has an empty progress cell and no commit or record names it since 2026-11-07, although one of its four parts (a brace button on pads) is in fact done on the Arena layout.
The Simple controller layout binds no brace button, so whether the 'Button only' brace style leaves a Simple-layout player without a brace is not evidenced.
Nothing written says the Alpha is English only, the game has no language choice, and the translation tools and the stretched-text test copy run in no CI job.
findings.orb: Is the Alpha English only? Recommended: yes, and say so in the tester guide.

There is no screen reader or menu narration: the area's own audit found no text-to-speech call, and a search of ui/ and render/ at the baseline finds none.

findings.s: Nothing for itch.io exists: no page set-up note, key procedure, channel names, upload script or rehearsal record (the same hole as TOOLS F-TOOLS-02, seen from the distribution side).
findings.orb: Will you create the itch.io account and the key-only page, and install its upload tool, yourself once Tools has a one-page checklist? Recommendation: yes, in one sitting.
findings.vnote: The only itch.io text outside the audit and the specification is Legal's and Marketing's disclosure, account and plan notes; none is a page set-up note, key procedure, channel list, upload script or rehearsal record. The upload-tool commands exist only in the audit's own web-checks table.

findings.s: There is no fixed shot list: the recipe file covers three of the six named shots and has no recipe for a transformation, a lap of the globe or a LAN 2v2 moment.
findings.vnote: Recipes exist for a beam struggle (:57), a launch through towers (:61) and a building fall (:66); the hook has a transform scenario and clips.json:29 names a transform event, but no recipe uses either, the only globe entry is a mockup (:70-72) and nothing films LAN play. The only 'shot list' pages are Camera's in-game camera designs, not a milestone list.

findings.s: No job renders the shots at a milestone and no archive exists: clips land in a git-ignored folder with no milestone name, no line on what changed and no backup.
findings.orb: Where is the progress archive kept safe? Recommendation: a second disk or a private folder you already have, copied at each milestone.
findings.vnote: Output goes to homework/Files/clips/<build folder>/, which is git-ignored, and no workflow or script runs the kit per milestone. The folder is named for a build folder, not a milestone, and no change line or backup note exists.

findings.s: The capture hook exists only in a browser build, so the Alpha candidate's own Windows and Linux programs cannot be filmed, and a LAN 2v2 shot depends on a replay route whose self-test is in no workflow and which has not yet read a real LAN save.
findings.vnote: The hook attaches only when OS.has_feature("web") holds, and lan-clip takes a kept web build of the same commit. The self-test file exists but no workflow runs it, and questions.md:16 lists the first real LAN save through lan-report as still owed by Tools.

findings.s: Footage is made at 960 by 540, shrunk to 480 wide at 12 pictures a second, as GIF or browser-recorded WebM with no MP4, below what the project's own Steam note asks of screenshots and a trailer.
findings.orb: May Tools ask you to install a free video encoder when the first teaser is cut? Recommendation: not now; keep full-size picture sequences until Beta is in sight.
findings.vnote: The facts hold (960 by 540 pictures, 480 wide, 12 a second, GIF or WebM, no MP4, against a note asking 1920 by 1080 screenshots and an MP4-family trailer), but size, width and frame rate are recipe defaults in data that a recipe can raise without code. The Steam sizes bind at Beta, not Alpha, so this does not make Alpha ship badly.

findings.s: Only GIFs get the flash check; WebM video and PNG sequences leave the kit with no verdict, and no page says how a public video is screened.
findings.vnote: flashVerdict is called only under format === 'gif'; the WebM paths (:282, :349) and PNG sequences write an index line with no verdict. Legal's pages say a trailer is read before it goes live but none says how a video file gets a flash reading.

findings.s: No tester guide says how a tester gets a key, installs on a Steam Deck, updates, or posts a report; the only tester page is Legal's note, which does not mention itch.io.
findings.vnote: No tester guide exists and Legal's note has nothing on itch.io, installing, a Steam Deck or updating. One fact is too strong: the note does name the report route (docs/legal/alpha-tester-note.md:29, the owner's private Discord server) and mentions a download key (:12), though not how to get or use one.

findings.orb: May the key-only page go up under the working title before the paid title search? Recommendation: yes, only if Legal first writes one row saying an unlisted, unpromoted, key-only page is acceptable.

The specification's 'not needed for a restricted itch.io page; confirm with Legal' is a question with no answer on record.

findings.s: The clips shared so far were staged on a private test copy with behaviour the game does not have (both at top power, a beam on a button, changed speeds, a scratch-only camera), so they cannot be remade from main and are not the game as played.
findings.vnote: The clips' own index lists top power, B firing the beam, ricochets on, a scratch follow camera, scripted blows and changed speeds, and the camera words exist only in a patch marked 'SCRATCH ONLY, never for main'. Nuance: the patch is kept so the clips can be remade on a scratch tree of 6a30b4c9, so 'cannot be remade' holds for main only, and the index calls them clips for a text message, not store assets.

findings.s: No rule says what happens to a shot when an old replay stops playing: a replay is refused on different data, and the page word that plays a saved match is a scratch patch, not game code on main.

The marketing plan predates Orb's Alpha definition: it stages a public browser build and public itch.io page, advises against Discord, still holds clips for the old placeholder names, and has no timeline counting back from the Steam demo.
findings.orb: What should 'Beta in sight' mean, the point where the Steam clock starts? Recommendation: four fighters playable on the Windows and Linux builds and the Alpha testers' reports folded in.

findings.s: The project's notes disagree with each other on Valve's waiting period and are stale on the licence: three records name different pages for the 21 and 30 days, and two Legal pages still call the code MIT.
The self-tests of the clip kit, the browser launcher and the LAN clip tool run in no workflow, so the chain the archive depends on can break unseen.
Bystanders' run cycles follow the shader's clock, not the tick, so two renders of the same shot differ in the crowd and a side-by-side shows a difference that is not a change in the game.
findings.vnote: crowd.gdshader drives the run, startle and bob cycles from TIME, and side-by-side.mjs takes capture-web frames with no freeze or mask for the crowd (its same-match check covers scenario, seed, pairing and variant only). The limit is documented in three places but nothing on main removes it.

findings.orb: Photo mode after Alpha? Recommendation: yes, after Alpha; the scripted shot list does not need it.
